appearance_facts.fact: Chart title is 'Monthly Reservoir Release Volume'.
Y-axis scale ranges from 0 to 40,000 in increments of 5,000, with tick marks at 10,000, 15,000, 20,000, 25,000, 30,000, and 35,000.
All bars are solid dark red.
Bars are evenly spaced along the x-axis.
Chart is horizontal bar chart with months on the x-axis and release volume on the y-axis.

printed_facts.fact: Bar heights correspond to release volumes: April ~30,000 m3, January ~40,000 m3, June ~17,500 m3, February ~20,000 m3, March ~27,000 m3, May ~8,000 m3.
The bar for May is the shortest, visually corresponding to approximately 8,000 m3 on the y-axis.
Reference bars: April (30,000 m3), January (40,000 m3), June (17,500 m3), February (20,000 m3), March (27,000 m3).

public_definitions: The goal is to review the monthly reservoir release dashboard and decide whether May should be handled as a standard low-release case or escalated as a critical low-release anomaly for this reporting cycle.
The chart reference is the monthly reservoir release dashboard.
The primary field label is 'May low-release route'.
The options are: Route May to standard low-release follow-up, Escalate May to critical low-release anomaly review, Send May to background monthly record filing.

The companion fields include: note, Program area (Water operations monitoring), Review scope (May low-release severity review), Record workflow (Low-release severity routing), Routing criterion (May low-release severity route).
